comment: Dr. Damer was an amazing professor, probably the best one I had yet. She grades easy and the total class grade is based on only a few things.
Professor Damar gives a lot of reading, and you have to do it to join class discussions. Participation is important, so I'm glad I don't have her next semester.

The pro was that taking Latin 201-2 with Dr. Damer meant I never needed to worry about my grade. She's knowledgeable and passionate, but the class isn't hard if you do the bare minimum. That said, she doesn't grade things on time, the class feels disorganized, and she gives crucial information last-minute. She's nice and an easy A, but frustrating.

Tons of reading, very much discussion-based. For the first exam, she provided a student-populated study guide, but the exam had questions that I never would've expected. Some may like her, but I personally would not recommend taking her class.

The class is very reading heavy for being a 101 class. I'm concurrently in clsc301 which takes about 1/4 to 1/5 the amount of time per class period prep-wise. The discussion topics so far are strongly tied to gender identity politics, so reading through that lens helps but ~60-70% of the assigned material doesn't tie to meaningful work.

Dr. Damer was bad, her lectures were all over the place and this class did not necessarily feel like a 101 class. There is so much reading, and even if you do it the discussions revolve around very complex ideas regarding a small portion of the text. Her exams have some questions that come out of left field.

Dr. Damer is an overall nice woman who cares for her students if her students reach out for help. However, the lectures are everywhere, and the order of the readings are disheveled, making it hard for someone who has never read Greek myths before or for any beginners. Tests are long and detailed, so be prepared for intricate questions.

CLSC101 fulfills the literature GenEd; expect a heavy reading load. Dr. Damer is caring, but she seems to jump all over the place with assigned excerpts, and she sometimes is disorganized. We return to previous works with no review, and it is hard to keep the plot straight. She teaches Gender Studies, and sometimes liberal ideologies carry over.

Fine class overall if you are looking for something for a Gen Ed/are interested in Mythology. There arent to many actual assignments, but you will have to read carefully if want to keep up with discussions. Midterms/papers can be tricky but if you have good notes and review should be fine. Only real complaint was that syllabus was kinda unclear.

Participation is a big part of your grade. Assignments were mostly readings that we discussed in class in addition to lecture topics. Tests were long and detailed, so be prepared to take good notes. Sometimes her lecture points her unclear, but overall a solid and interesting class.

Dr Damer's lectures were very interesting but there was a great deal of reading and sometimes it did not even correlate with the lectures. Lots of homework and reflection/ paper assignments in addition to the reading. She is VERY unclear about her grading criteria and her tests are long and some questions really come out of left field.
Very nice and understanding professor. She will make you earn the grade but is an extremely fair grader. She is more than willing to meet outside of class and is able to hold an engaging class.

Dr. Damer is a lot of fun, I took her for an into mythology course. Her lectures are interesting and generally discussion directed, however tests can be very complicated and very long, her class is also VERY reading intensive.
Dr. Damer is really awesome and caring. The FYS I took with her, gender, violence, & Rome, was not my topic of interest but she made the class doable. as long as you try you will be okay!

I love the topic of the course, but I thoroughly and truly hate this professor. She grades the course as if it were a 300 course and is very unclear on her grading criteria. The classwork and essays have no correlation; you may feel like you're breezing through and getting everything, but your essay grades will say otherwise.
